title.value: The functional specialization of visual cortex emerges from training parallel pathways with self-supervised predictive learning
title.justification: The title directly addresses the main focus of the paper - understanding how functional specialization in the visual cortex can be achieved by training networks with self-supervised predictive learning.
title.quote: The functional specialization of visual cortex emerges from training parallel pathways with self-supervised predictive learning

analysis.description: This paper investigates the modeling of both ventral ("what") and dorsal ("where") pathways of the visual cortex using a single deep neural network trained with a self-supervised predictive loss function. It utilizes the Contrastive Predictive Coding (CPC) technique on an architecture with parallel pathways and evaluates its performance on datasets involving both mouse visual cortex and video-based tasks.

type.justification: The paper focuses on computational experiments and models trained using neural data, particularly highlighting empirical results from comparing model predictions with brain recordings.
type.quote: We show that when we train a deep neural network architecture with two parallel pathways using a self-supervised predictive loss function, we can outperform other models in fitting mouse visual cortex.

name.justification: The research models visual processing in the cortex, leveraging insights from neuroscience to inform computational architectures and training techniques.
name.quote: Our work demonstrates the importance of self-supervised predictive learning for generating ventral- and dorsal-like representations, showing an interaction between the architecture and learning rule.

name.justification: The paper specifically uses self-supervised predictive learning as a central paradigm for training the ANNs to model visual pathways.
name.quote: Altogether, this work demonstrates that the two specialized pathways of visual cortex can be modelled with the same ANN if a self-supervised predictive loss function is applied to an architecture with parallel pathways.

name.justification: This specific method of self-supervised learning is central to the paper's experiments.
name.quote: We use the CPC loss function for self-supervised learning, which was developed for modeling sequential data, including video datasets.

name.justification: The one-pathway version of the ResNet architecture used to evaluate single-pathway representation in visual processing.
name.quote: The one-pathway ResNet (ResNet-1p) is a regular 3D ResNet (Figure 2a).

is_contributed.justification: This model configuration is analyzed and compared as part of the research findings on single-pathway specialization.
is_contributed.quote: When we train a network with a single pathway, we find that it possesses more ventral-like representations.

is_executed.justification: The model is executed and its results are analyzed with respect to its similarity to brain recordings.
is_executed.quote: ...we compare the similarity of RSMs between ResNet-1p trained with CPC and the dorsal areas (VISam and VISal).

is_compared.justification: ResNet-1p is compared for its representational fit against several other models including multi-pathway architectures.
is_compared.quote: Comparing the maximum representational similarities between models...

name.justification: The two-pathway version of the ResNet architecture used to demonstrate specialization along visual processing pathways.
name.quote: The two-pathway ResNet (ResNet-2p) is composed of two parallel ResNet branches, which split after a single convolutional layer.

is_contributed.quote: We choose this ResNet-2p architecture... to check whether ResNet-2p can learn both ventral- and dorsal-like representations.
